bioAdditions:
The SAR Patriot Research System entry P-232580 now shows five approved member applications: three already known (1995, 2014, 2017) and two approved in late 2025 - Joshua Paul Lance (NJ, 10 Oct 2025, via son James) and Brian Tyler Baker (PA, 7 Nov 2025, via son Daniel) (S1). None descends through Martha (Pringle), so Johnny's line would be a new line for SAR/DAR; the existing applications can be bought from SAR for their proofs of Thomas's service. The SAR page records burial at Shupp's Cemetery, Larksville, but notes 'No entry found in Find-A-Grave - Nov 2024'.

The page also carries a user-contributed biography (author Robert Stanley Ptaszek) that should not be relied on. It names Thomas's mother as 'Marie (Dubois)', lists children (John m. Sarah Holland, Samuel m. Martha Baker, Mary m. James Hicks, Jacob, Abigail, Rebecca...) that do not match Thomas's own 1815 will, has him moving to Luzerne 'about 1805' (he was in Plymouth by 1790 and in the 1800 census) and as a Luzerne justice 1813-17, and cites a 'Revolutionary-War Pension File NY-RWP-00123' showing a reduction to corporal in 1779. That citation is not in the form of a federal pension file number (S/W/R), no such pension appears in the indexes searched, and Thomas died in 1829, before the 1832 act under which most militia veterans applied (S1). It should be treated as unsupported. Separately, the published New York in the Revolution (1898) lists Isaac Lamore, John Lamoreux and Nicolas Lamarux - but not Thomas - among the Orange County First Regiment land-bounty-rights men, alongside Benjamin and David Prindle (S2).
openQuestionsNew: Widow's pension: Keturah lived until c.1842; check NARA M804 (Fold3 index) for any W- or R- file under Thomas Lamoreux/Lamoree - none found in web search.
Purchase SAR application ACN 75326 (2017, via Thomas Jr.) and ACN 119145 (2025, via Daniel) to see what proof of service was accepted.
Birth year: his mother appears to have been unmarried in 1746 (see Charity Davenport H0073), so 'abt 1745' needs checking against his age at death or in the census.
